trials.notes: Used the right structural API: WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag(), get_tag(), get_breadcrumbs(), add_class(), and get_updated_html(). All are documented in the rendered files. The implementation follows the documented breadcrumb pattern and relies on add_class()/get_updated_html() for byte-preserving class edits. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Used WP_HTML_Processor and only documented methods. Token walking with next_token(), get_token_type(), and is_tag_closer() is valid, but slightly less direct than next_tag() for a tag-only mutation. The extra breadcrumb count check is redundant because create_fragment() breadcrumbs include HTML and BODY, but it does not change the result. No _doing_it_wrong records.

Used the right processor and documented structural methods. The main near-miss is the final fallback on paused_at_incomplete_token()/get_last_error(): it is documented and defensible as a fail-closed policy, but for this contract it can discard valid earlier class edits when the input has trailing incomplete syntax. No _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 7 frozen cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute to a documentation failure. The docs performed well on the core decision: html-processor.md explicitly says WP_HTML_Processor adds structural awareness, nesting depth, ancestor breadcrumbs, implied/virtual closing tags, and should be chosen whenever document structure matters. The get_breadcrumbs() section also made the current-node-included breadcrumb model discoverable, which led all trials to detect list ancestry correctly. The add_class() and get_updated_html() documentation successfully steered subjects toward byte-preserving class edits instead of serialization or string rewriting. Near-misses: trial 2 used a full token walk even though next_tag() is the simpler documented pattern for opener-only tag edits; trial 3 applied an over-conservative incomplete-input fallback that would drop earlier valid edits on inputs such as a nested list followed by an incomplete trailing comment.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that breadcrumbs include HTML/BODY and the current node, but they do not give a compact idiom for asking whether the current element has an ancestor matching a condition. This invites redundant depth/count guards or off-by-one reasoning.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that ancestors are `array_slice( $processor->get_breadcrumbs(), 0, -1 )`, and that application-level ancestry checks should usually ignore the implicit HTML/BODY entries unless those are explicitly relevant.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain both walkers, but tag-only mutations can still lead readers to choose next_token() plus token-type and closer guards.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a brief cross-reference in next_token(): for edits that only need element openers, prefer `next_tag()` because it skips closers by default; reserve `next_token()` for text, comments, serialization, or mixed-token rewrites.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say callers should choose a fallback policy for incomplete input, but they do not spell out that queued attribute/class edits remain available through get_updated_html() even after a later incomplete trailing token.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that `paused_at_incomplete_token()` reports scan completeness, not loss of queued edits. Document the tradeoff between returning `get_updated_html()` with earlier edits preserved versus returning the original input under a fail-closed contract.
